title: Artificial intelligence in education
text: Artificial intelligence in education The wide possibilities of information processing and knowledge production using generative artificial intelligence have potentially huge consequences for education, as they reproduce higher-order thinking, which is the basis of human learning. The paper’s objective is to analyze the directions of modern use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education. AI in education is used to personalize learning (adaptive platforms), automate routine tasks (reporting, lesson plans) for teachers, generate educational content (learning materials, presentations), as well as helping students through chatbots and virtual assistants that provide instant support and explanations. Scientists categorize AI-robots into «mindful» (AI-robots with increasingly human characteristics) and «mindless» (AI-robots with machine characteristics) tools. «Mindless» robots: text generators, spelling assistants, interactive and gamified materials. «Mindful» AI-robots: chatbots, virtual avatars, social-humanoid robots. The introduction of AI into education has its own challenges and risks. One such challenge is the weak connection between theoretical and pedagogical perspectives and the practical application of AI in the classroom. Ethical and educational approaches to AI are also under investigation. Higher education institutions must adapt their policies to new technologies, while simultaneously implementing learning analytics tools to improve learning environments, reduce student dropout rates, and adapt their curricula. Future teachers are well-placed to address the challenges posed by AI in education and explore effective ways to integrate these tools into the classroom. Conclusions: AI should not displace humans from their intellectual role. AI will help us open new perspectives in education and serve as a basis for collective thinking and joint action that can lead to the creation of a future digital educational environment that is human-centered and accessible to everyone.

title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Education
text: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Education Artificial intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing education, improving personalized learning, automating administrative tasks and increasing student engagement. As AI-based technologies such as machine learning, natural language processing, and adaptive learning systems evolve, their integration into educational environments is transforming traditional teaching methods. This article explores the impact of artificial intelligence on education, analysing both its potential benefits and challenges. The primary data collection tool was an online survey, developed and distributed via Google Forms during spring 2025. The questionnaire included rating scales, single-choice, and multiple-choice questions focused on familiarity and usage of AI, perceived benefits and risks, and evaluations of effectiveness. A total of 100 respondents, primarily drawn from higher education (students, teachers, academic staff) and supplemented by participants from secondary education. This sample reflects a variety of roles and educational backgrounds, ensuring a multi-perspective view. The survey explored knowledge and practical experience with AI-powered tools in education; effectiveness of specific tools (chatbots, adaptive systems, automated grading, etc.); and perceptions of benefits, challenges, ethical issues, and prospects for AI integration. The research used descriptive statistics to interpret results. Most respondents were familiar with AI and had used AI-powered tools in educational settings. Most agreed that AI positively impacts education, especially in areas like personalized and adaptive learning, automated grading and feedback, chatbots for student support, data-driven performance prediction, and reducing administrative workload for teachers. At the same time, concerns about privacy, bias, decreased human interaction, inequality of access, and over-reliance on technology were consistently rated as significant. These findings demonstrate that while AI is widely seen as beneficial, its integration must be managed thoughtfully to address associated risks.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Education: Investigating Teacher Attitudes
text: Artificial Intelligence in Education: Investigating Teacher Attitudes This study aims to investigate teachers' attitudes towards AI in education, focusing on identifying the perceived benefits, challenges, and ethical considerations associated with AI integration into teaching and learning environments. Utilizing a qualitative research design, this study conducted semi-structured interviews with 28 educators from various educational levels and disciplines. Thematic analysis was employed to analyze the interview data, identifying key themes and concepts related to teachers' perspectives on AI in education. Four main themes were identified: Pedagogical Impacts, Ethical and Social Considerations, Technological Challenges and Opportunities, and Perceptions of AI in Education. Pedagogical Impacts encompassed enhancing learning outcomes, curriculum integration, and the evolving roles of teachers. Ethical and Social Considerations highlighted concerns over data privacy, bias, and equity. Technological Challenges and Opportunities discussed integration challenges and the future of educational technology. Lastly, Perceptions of AI in Education revealed varied attitudes, awareness levels, and perceived impacts on professional identity. Teachers recognize the transformative potential of AI in enhancing personalized learning and operational efficiency. However, concerns about ethical issues, technological infrastructure, and the need for professional development are significant. Addressing these concerns requires targeted efforts from policymakers, educational leaders, and technologists to foster a supportive environment for AI integration in education.
